status_summary: HUD Mortgagee Letter 2025-08, issued 2025-03-19 and effective immediately, rescinded the FHA appraisal letters ML 2024-07, ML 2024-16 and ML 2021-27 and restored the earlier appraisal requirements. On 2025-07-10 HUD and OMB announced the end of policies introduced under the PAVE task force, effectively disbanding it, and stated that the Fair Housing Act and the Equal Credit Opportunity Act continue to be enforced. A HUD Office of General Counsel notice published 2026-07-17 (91 FR 44867) withdrew 13 guidance documents, including the 2022 appraisal elements of proof guidance, effective 2025-09-25. The changes rest on rescinded letters and withdrawn guidance rather than rulemaking.

timeline.event: HUD Mortgagee Letter 2025-08, effective immediately, rescinded ML 2024-07, ML 2024-16 and ML 2021-27 and restored prior FHA single family appraisal requirements, pending an update to Handbook 4000.1.

HUD and OMB announced the termination of the PAVE-era FHA mortgagee letters on appraisal review, reconsideration of value and appraiser fair housing compliance, effectively disbanding the PAVE task force.
HUD published a notice (91 FR 44867) withdrawing 13 guidance documents, including the 2022 appraisal elements of proof guidance, effective 2025-09-25.

uncertainties: Mortgagee Letter 2025-08 and the HUD release of 2025-07-10 were read in full on hud.gov in review, and the 2026 OGC notice was read on govinfo.gov by the researcher; mortgagee letters are not published in the Federal Register. The release describes the task force as effectively disbanded in its headline but does not state a formal dissolution. The HUD superseded-documents page lists ML 2024-07 and ML 2021-27 as superseded but gives no supersession dates and omits ML 2024-16. The 2026 OGC notice does not mention PAVE, so it is recorded as a related guidance withdrawal. Whether Handbook 4000.1 was formally updated was not checked. The Mandate recommendation also covers other appraisal-integrity actions beyond PAVE, which were not separately searched. Trade and law-firm accounts (National Association of Realtors, Orrick, HousingWire) are consistent with the HUD documents.
